The purpose of this notebook is to explore the results from the storm surge
exposure analysis. For each of 4 CMIP6 models we compute the change in 100-year
return period storm surge level (future 2021-2050 minus historical 1985-2014).
Each NPS water supply is assigned the worst-case model surge change from its
nearest coastal station, divided by distance to coast. Water supplies whose
nearest surge station is more than 50 km away receive NA.

Data are generated in `rapid_workflow.Rmd` using `calc_storm_surge_exposure()`.
Raw surge stations are preprocessed by `process_storm_surge_data()`.

# Interpretation

Two complementary metrics are computed for each water supply:

`raw_surge_change_max` is the absolute change in the 100-year return period
(RP100) surge height (in meters) at the nearest coastal model node, computed as
future (2021–2050) minus historical (1985–2014) under SSP5-8.5, divided by
`coast_dist_m` (distance to coast in meters).

`raw_surge_pct_change_max` is the same change expressed as a percentage of the
historical RP100 surge level — `(future - historical) / historical * 100` —
also divided by `coast_dist_m`. This metric normalizes by baseline surge
magnitude, making it more comparable across locations with different historical
surge levels.

Both metrics weight exposure by coastal proximity: the same surge change matters
more for a supply close to the coast than one near the 50 km boundary. In
practice, the distance weighting dominates the final rankings because the range
of variation in `coast_dist_m` far exceeds the range of variation in surge
change. A supply 50 m from the coast gets a divisor of 50 (multiplier ~0.02);
one at 5,000 m gets a divisor of 5,000 (multiplier ~0.0002) — a 100x difference
in weight from distance alone. Absolute surge changes across all CONUS stations
typically vary by only 5–10x. Distance variation therefore swamps surge
variation, and the final ordering is determined almost entirely by coastal
proximity rather than projected surge change magnitude. An alternative weighting
approach — a 0-to-1 decay function that approaches 0 as distance approaches
50 km — bounds the weight range to roughly 5x, which would allow surge magnitude
to play a larger role in rankings.

The worst-case value across the 4 CMIP6 models is retained for each station, so
both metrics reflect the most adverse projected outcome rather than a model mean.

The metrics capture only the *change in surge dynamics* driven by altered storm
climatology; they do not include mean sea level rise, which is addressed
separately by the sea level rise inundation indicator.

Water supplies more than 50 km from the nearest coastal surge station receive
`NA` — they are considered outside the domain of meaningful coastal surge
exposure regardless of surge magnitude at the nearest station.

# Data source

Source: Muis et al. (2023), distributed through the Copernicus Climate Data
Store (CDS), dataset `storm_surge_muis_2023/` (local path).

## What was downloaded

| Field | Value | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| **Model** | CMCC-CM2-VHR4, EC-Earth3P-HR, HadGEM3-GC31-HM, HadGEM3-GC31-HM-SST | High-resolution HighResMIP models — chosen because coarse models underestimate tropical cyclone-driven surges |
| **Period** | 1985–2014 (historical), 2021–2050 (future) | Historical baseline vs. near-future projection window |
| **Variable** | Surge level | Meteorological surge component in meters — not total water level, not SLR |
| **Statistic** | 100-year return period (RP100), best-fit bound | Upper-tail surge height representative of a 1-in-100-year event over each 30-year period |
| **Experiment** | Historical, Future | Historical = ERA5-forced run; Future = SSP5-8.5 forced run |
| **Derived variable** | Absolute value | Actual surge height in meters — not already a change value; the change is computed in `process_storm_surge_data()` |

## What we are trying to calculate: 

How much storm surge is projected to change at 
a given water supply. We are not considering tides and mean sea level rise as a 
part of this analysis. 

## How we are calculating this risk: 

The Global Tide and Surge Model v3.0 (GTSM) is 
a 2D hydrodynamic model. For each climate model run, hourly wind speed and surface
pressure fields are used to force GTSM, which sumulates the resulting surge height
at ~43,000 coastal stations globally (roughly one every ~5-10km along coastlines).

Over each 30-year period GTSM produces a time series of hourly surge heights at
each coastal station. The 100-year return period (RP100) is the surge height
expected to be exceeded on average once every 100 years — an extreme but
plausible event.

For each of the 4 models, `process_storm_surge_data()` computes:

```
surge_change = future_rp100 (2021–2050) − historical_rp100 (1985–2014)
```

The worst-case value across the 4 models is retained per station. 
`calc_storm_surge_exposure()` then assigns each water supply the surge change 
from its nearest station, with a 50 km distance cutoff.

# Establish environment

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r}
source("setup.R")
mapviewOptions(fgb = FALSE)
```

# Load data

## Water supplies

```{r}
water_supplies <- get_wsd(rapid = TRUE)
```

## Storm surge stations (preprocessed CONUS subset)

```{r}
storm_surge_stations <- sf::st_read(
  here("data", "rapid", "inputs", "storm_surge", "storm_surge_exposure_conus.gpkg"),
  quiet = TRUE
)
```

## Storm surge exposure results

Check for a saved CSV first; fall back to running the calc function if none exists.

```{r}
exp_files <- list.files(
  here("data", "rapid", "outputs"),
  pattern    = "^storm_surge_exposure_.*\\.csv$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

if (length(exp_files) > 0) {
  storm_surge_exp <- read_csv(exp_files[length(exp_files)], show_col_types = FALSE)
} else {
  storm_surge_exp <- calc_storm_surge_exposure(
    water_supplies       = water_supplies,
    storm_surge_stations = here("data", "rapid", "inputs", "storm_surge",
                                "storm_surge_exposure_conus.gpkg"),
    save       = TRUE,
    output_dir = here("data", "rapid", "outputs"),
    verbose    = TRUE
  )
}
```

## Join results to water supply geometries

```{r}
ws_mapped <- water_supplies %>%
  inner_join(
    storm_surge_exp %>% select(-park_unit, -park_name),
    by = "wsd_source_id"
  )
```

# Maps

## Water supplies and nearest surge station connections (absolute change)

Water supply points are colored by normalized absolute surge change. Each
coastal water supply is connected by a line to the surge station used to assign
its value. Surge stations are colored by `max_surge_change_m` — stations matched
to at least one water supply are shown; unmatched stations are grey. Water
supplies more than 50 km from the nearest surge station are grey.

```{r}
pal <- colorRampPalette(c("green", "yellow", "red"))

ws_exposed <- ws_mapped %>% filter(!is.na(raw_surge_change_max))
ws_distant <- ws_mapped %>% filter(is.na(raw_surge_change_max))

# Project for nearest-neighbor geometry, then build connector lines
ws_exposed_proj      <- st_transform(ws_exposed, 5070)
stations_proj_albers <- st_transform(storm_surge_stations, 5070)

nearest_idx     <- st_nearest_feature(ws_exposed_proj, stations_proj_albers)
used_idx        <- unique(nearest_idx)
stations_used   <- stations_proj_albers[used_idx, ]   %>% st_transform(4326)
stations_unused <- stations_proj_albers[-used_idx, ]  %>% st_transform(4326)

connector_lines <- st_nearest_points(
  ws_exposed_proj,
  stations_proj_albers[nearest_idx, ],
  pairwise = TRUE
) %>%
  st_as_sf() %>%
  st_transform(4326)

mapview(stations_unused,
        col.regions = "grey60",
        color       = "grey60",
        cex         = 3,
        layer.name  = "Surge stations (unmatched)") +
  mapview(connector_lines,
          color      = "black",
          lwd        = 1,
          layer.name = "WS → surge station") +
  mapview(stations_used,
          zcol        = "max_surge_change_m",
          col.regions = pal,
          color       = NA,
          cex         = 5,
          pch         = 18,
          layer.name  = "Surge stations (matched)",
          popup       = leafpop::popupTable(
            sf::st_drop_geometry(stations_used) %>%
              select(lon, lat, max_surge_change_m, max_surge_pct_change, max_surge_model)
          )) +
  mapview(ws_exposed,
          zcol        = "norm_surge_change_max",
          col.regions = pal,
          layer.name  = "Storm Surge Change (norm)",
          popup       = leafpop::popupTable(
            sf::st_drop_geometry(ws_exposed) %>%
              select(wsd_source_id, park_name,
                     raw_surge_change_max,
                     norm_surge_change_max,
                     rank_surge_change_max)
          )) +
  mapview(ws_distant,
          col.regions = "grey60",
          color       = "grey60",
          layer.name  = ">50 km from surge station",
          popup       = leafpop::popupTable(
            sf::st_drop_geometry(ws_distant) %>%
              select(wsd_source_id, park_name,
                     raw_surge_change_max,
                     norm_surge_change_max,
                     rank_surge_change_max)
          ))
```

# Decay function weighting (alternative)

Instead of dividing by `coast_dist_m`, this approach multiplies the raw surge
value by a linear decay weight: `1 - (coast_dist_m / 50000)`. The weight is 1.0
at the shoreline and 0.0 at the 50 km cutoff, so the weight range is bounded to
0–1 (~5x variation). Because surge changes across CONUS stations vary by
5–10x, the two sources of variation are now comparable — surge magnitude plays a
meaningful role in rankings alongside coastal proximity.

## Build decay-weighted results

```{r}
coast_dist_df <- read_csv(
  here("data", "rapid", "inputs", "coast_comp", "coast_distances.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# nearest_idx and stations_proj_albers already built in the first map chunk
decay_results <- ws_exposed %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(wsd_source_id, park_unit, park_name) %>%
  mutate(
    surge_change_raw     = stations_proj_albers$max_surge_change_m[nearest_idx],
    surge_pct_change_raw = stations_proj_albers$max_surge_pct_change[nearest_idx]
  ) %>%
  left_join(coast_dist_df, by = c("wsd_source_id", "park_unit", "park_name")) %>%
  mutate(
    decay_weight                  = pmax(0, 1 - (coast_dist_m / 50000)),
    raw_surge_change_decay        = surge_change_raw     * decay_weight,
    raw_surge_pct_change_decay    = surge_pct_change_raw * decay_weight
  ) %>%
  select(wsd_source_id, park_unit, park_name,
         raw_surge_change_decay, raw_surge_pct_change_decay) %>%
  add_standardized_indicators("raw_surge_change_decay",     invert = FALSE) %>%
  add_standardized_indicators("raw_surge_pct_change_decay", invert = FALSE)

ws_decay <- water_supplies %>%
  left_join(decay_results, by = c("wsd_source_id", "park_unit", "park_name"))

ws_decay_exposed <- ws_decay %>% filter(!is.na(raw_surge_change_decay))
```

## Decay-weighted absolute surge change

```{r}
mapview(stations_unused,
        col.regions = "grey60",
        color       = "grey60",
        cex         = 3,
        layer.name  = "Surge stations (unmatched)") +
  mapview(connector_lines,
          color      = "black",
          lwd        = 1,
          layer.name = "WS → surge station") +
  mapview(stations_used,
          zcol        = "max_surge_change_m",
          col.regions = pal,
          color       = NA,
          cex         = 5,
          pch         = 18,
          layer.name  = "Surge stations (matched)",
          popup       = leafpop::popupTable(
            sf::st_drop_geometry(stations_used) %>%
              select(lon, lat, max_surge_change_m, max_surge_pct_change, max_surge_model)
          )) +
  mapview(ws_decay_exposed,
          zcol        = "norm_surge_change_decay",
          col.regions = pal,
          layer.name  = "Surge Change — decay weight (norm)",
          popup       = leafpop::popupTable(
            sf::st_drop_geometry(ws_decay_exposed) %>%
              select(wsd_source_id, park_name,
                     raw_surge_change_decay,
                     norm_surge_change_decay,
                     rank_surge_change_decay)
          )) +
  mapview(ws_distant,
          col.regions = "grey60",
          color       = "grey60",
          layer.name  = ">50 km from surge station",
          popup       = leafpop::popupTable(
            sf::st_drop_geometry(ws_distant) %>%
              select(wsd_source_id, park_name)
          ))
```

## Rank comparison: division vs. decay

Points on the diagonal have identical ranks under both methods. Points above
the line rank higher under decay weighting; points below rank lower. Color
shows the unweighted station value (raw surge change or percent change) —
this reveals whether rank shifts are driven by high-surge or low-surge stations.

```{r rank-comparison}
rank_comparison <- ws_exposed %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(wsd_source_id, park_name,
         rank_surge_change_max, rank_surge_pct_change_max) %>%
  left_join(
    decay_results %>% select(wsd_source_id,
                              rank_surge_change_decay,
                              rank_surge_pct_change_decay),
    by = "wsd_source_id"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    station_surge_change_m   = stations_proj_albers$max_surge_change_m[nearest_idx],
    station_surge_pct_change = stations_proj_albers$max_surge_pct_change[nearest_idx]
  )

p_abs <- ggplot(rank_comparison,
                aes(x = rank_surge_change_max, y = rank_surge_change_decay,
                    color = station_surge_change_m)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "grey60", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "grey80", high = "red", name = "Surge\nchange (m)") +
  labs(x = "Rank — division (current)", y = "Rank — decay",
       title = "Absolute surge change") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

p_pct <- ggplot(rank_comparison,
                aes(x = rank_surge_pct_change_max, y = rank_surge_pct_change_decay,
                    color = station_surge_pct_change)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "grey60", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "grey80", high = "red", name = "Surge\n% change") +
  labs(x = "Rank — division (current)", y = "Rank — decay",
       title = "Percent surge change") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

p_abs + p_pct
```
